heuristic.applicability: Prefer when the drawer is already open and the high-level agent can identify the current physical phase from the observed TCP, gripper, red, blue and goal relationships. In particular, prefer red_acquire when displacement of exposed red is the dominant change, red_place_release when the reachable outside pad has moved, and blue_acquire when the successor blue pickup pose has moved. Use drawer_clear at the closed-at-handle segment entry, then bridge_to_blue only after red has been released and the TCP has cleared vertically. The world/TCP phases deliberately avoid translating handle-clearance or post-release bridge motion with an unrelated object.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer_position is strictly above 0.26 m and red is exposed. The represented entry at action 230 can still have closed fingers and the TCP at the drawer front; call drawer_clear there. Later entry is allowed only when the caller selects the phase matching the observable relationship: red_acquire for approach/contact/lift near red, red_place_release while red is held and moving to or resting on the pad, bridge_to_blue after released-red clearance, or blue_acquire once transit/approach to blue is intended.
handoff.exit_conditions: Nominal exit is red fully contained on the outside pad at z about 0.020 m and no longer following the TCP, drawer_position still strictly above 0.26 m, and blue/TCP co-motion after a closed-finger pickup and initial lift. These are switch cues; release, co-motion and finger state do not change the fixed evaluator rule.
handoff.failure_signatures: Wrong-phase invocation can create a frame discontinuity, target the wrong object, or issue wrong gripper behavior. Other signatures are red failing to co-move after closure, carried red moving low into furniture, red outside the pad, red still following after release, failure to clear red before bridge_to_blue, transit redirected to red, blue absent under the TCP, closed fingers without blue/TCP co-motion, IK non-convergence, or drawer_position falling toward the strict 0.26 m boundary.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions remain supervised exactly once. Actions [230,470) provide 240 actions per demonstration shared with open_drawer: drawer_clear plus red approach/contact and early lift. Actions [600,850) provide 250 actions per demonstration shared with blue_insert: final goal-centered red descent/release, post-release bridge, and blue-centered transit/contact/lift. This preserves 2,880 predecessor-overlap and 3,000 successor-overlap actions across 12 demonstrations.
handoff.successor_readiness: blue_insert may enter from action 600 while red is still held/touching the pad because the overlap explicitly supervises red release first. A cleaner switch is after blue is under the TCP, fingers are closed near the demonstrated width, and blue/TCP co-motion shows initial lift, as at the later part of blue_acquire near action 850.

heuristic.limitations: This is phase-routed equivariance, not recovery. The caller must choose the correct phase from physical observations; a wrong or premature switch changes coordinate semantics. Anchors are frozen for each sampled chunk, so fast anchor motion or stale/noisy object poses can bias all eight executed slots. The 50-action bridge phase has less supervision and is only local-TCP-relative, so it is not by construction invariant to a large blue displacement until blue_acquire. Large red/goal/blue moves can be unreachable or obstructed, and no collision planner is added. Demonstrations do not establish recovery from a missed grasp, off-pad release, unintended drawer contact, or changed grasp physics. Mixed phase semantics may reduce data efficiency relative to h02 despite the intended invariances.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Publish red_transfer__h04 as an independent model next to h01-h03. The high-level agent must provide one of five semantic phases and the fixed identifiers, retaining causal history across switches. Prefer h02 as the observed strong in-distribution fallback when phase confidence is low; prefer h04 when a reliable displaced red, red_goal or blue pose makes the corresponding semantic anchor useful. Terminate or hand off from physical red-on-pad/drawer-open and blue-lift cues, never from an elapsed-time counter. No original policy or success rule changes.
heuristic.rationale: The fixed validation observed h02 at 10/12 with zero unconverged IK steps, while its two failures kept the drawer open but left red off the pad. h01's all-segment red frame passed 4/12 and had 2,866 unconverged IK steps; h03's all-segment local TCP frame passed 9/12 but its three failures included drawer closure. The new prior therefore does not replace the stable global references everywhere. It routes Cartesian targets to the semantic anchor relevant to each responsibility: world for handle clearance, red for acquisition, red_goal for transport/place/release, chunk TCP for a short bridge, and blue for successor acquisition. In inspected demo1000/1001, action 300 is high and clear, 320-500 covers red approach through elevated lift, 500-650 covers goal transport/release/vertical retreat, 650-700 is a clear transit bridge, and 700-850 reaches and lifts blue. Red- and blue-frame phases make approached-object displacement equivariant by construction at the Cartesian label/decoder level; goal centering makes placement translate with the observed pad. Configuration, fingers, velocities and drawer state remain inputs, so reachability/contact dependencies are retained. Expected OOD benefit is unconfirmed.
heuristic.statement: Phase-routed semantic-anchor Cartesian Diffusion Policy: learn a uniform 10-D TCP target [anchor-frame XYZ, anchor-frame rotation 6D, gripper], but select the causal anchor by high-level physical phase—world, red SE(3), red_goal translation, current TCP SE(3), or blue SE(3). This targets red/goal/blue displacement without forcing drawer clearance or the red-to-blue bridge into an unrelated object frame.

subgoal: Primary responsibility: after the drawer is open, acquire the exposed red block, lift and carry it to the marked outside pad, lower it, release it, and retreat. The segment then intentionally continues through the approach, contact, grasp, and initial lift of the blue block for the next handoff. Observed contact/motion: the red block is pinched with fingers near 0.018 m, carried at roughly 0.30 m height, lowered to the pad, released as the fingers open, and left at z about 0.020 m; the TCP retreats before crossing to blue. Entry observation 230 has drawer_position 0.300, TCP still at the drawer front, and fingers near 0.007 m, so the skill is supervised to release/retract before acquiring red. At exit observation 850, red is already on the pad and blue is gripped with fingers near 0.018 m and lifted to z about 0.061-0.193 m, depending on occurrence. Examples: demo1000 indices 470/560/600/610 show red lift, carry, pad descent, and release; 700/800/850 show retreat, blue approach, and blue lift. Images at demo1000 indices 560, 610, 800, and 850 support the pad and blue-pickup interpretation. Purpose/expected benefit: this isolates red placement while retaining both adjacent transitions; overlap is expected to reduce sensitivity to switching before red grasp or before blue grasp, but it does not demonstrate recovery from an off-pad release.
